document.title: MDM Reproduction Training Run - Technical Plan
document.purpose: External technical review before launching a ~31h GPU training run

objective.primary: Retrain Motion Diffusion Model (MDM) from scratch on HumanML3D to reproduce the shipped humanml_enc_512_50steps checkpoint
objective.rationale: The goal is to validate the training PIPELINE, not to improve the model. Targeting a known-good result yields a pass/fail signal. If the reproduction matches the reference, the pipeline is trustworthy and later experiments inherit that trust. If it diverges, we learn it on a run whose correct answer is already known.
objective.secondary: Own a set of weights trained by us from a public dataset, removing dependence on a third-party checkpoint (licensing position)

throughput_measured.note: Independently validates against MDM paper's '~3 days on a 2080 Ti': 750000 * 0.417s = 86.8h = 3.6 days

throughput_measured.method: live 383-step training epoch, full training loop including optimizer step and dataloading

reasons: Its real advantage is batch size (512+ vs 64); raising batch size changes gradient noise and requires LR re-tuning, i.e. changes the recipe, defeating the stated objective
At batch 64 a large card is badly under-utilised; speedup would come only from clock and memory bandwidth, not occupancy
rejected_alternative.revisit_when: the next run, where a changed recipe is the point rather than a contaminant

cost_projection.eval_overhead_basis: measured 75s per save+eval+gen cycle at eval_num_samples=320, eval_rep_times=1; full protocol is 1000 samples * 3 reps = 9.375x eval work; 12 evals total
cost_projection.eval_overhead_uncertainty: MDM prints a hardcoded 'Should take about 90 min' warning which, if accurate for the full protocol, would imply 18h of eval overhead instead. Our measurement suggests otherwise but this is the largest uncertainty in the estimate.

recipe.source: verbatim from reference checkpoint save/humanml_enc_512_50steps/args.json unless listed in deviations

loss_weights.consequence: All geometric losses are zero, so the loss is plain MSE on the 263-dim HML vector. Rotation2xyz / SMPL is never invoked in the training math.

periodic.expected_checkpoints_correction: Previously stated as 12. Verified from training_loop.py: saves fire when total_step() % save_interval == 0, which for steps 0..600161 gives 13 saves (0, 50k, ..., 600k inclusive), plus a final save because (600161-1) % 50000 = 160 != 0. Total 14 saves and 14 evaluations.
periodic.multimodality_note: run_mm=False is hardcoded at training_loop.py:263, so MultiModality is never computed during training. The 'MultiModality Summary' header still prints but emits no values and no key appears in the results dict. It MUST be evaluated post-hoc from a saved checkpoint if wanted.

num_steps_semantics.finding: num_steps does NOT terminate the training loop. It is used only to compute num_epochs = num_steps // len(data) + 1, and the loop then runs that many COMPLETE epochs. The only in-loop break is on lr_anneal_steps, which is unset.
num_steps_semantics.corroborating_evidence: The pre-flight validation was launched with num_steps=60 and ran to step 383 - exactly one full epoch - confirming the loop ignores num_steps as a stopping condition.
num_steps_semantics.resume_behaviour: num_epochs is computed from num_steps alone and IGNORES resume_step, while total_step() = step + resume_step. So on a resume, num_steps behaves as ADDITIONAL steps layered on top of the resumed position.

recipe.launch_command: python -m train.train_mdm --save_dir /workspace/checkpoints/repro_full --dataset humanml --arch trans_enc --diffusion_steps 50 --noise_schedule cosine --latent_dim 512 --layers 8 --batch_size 64 --lr 1e-4 --weight_decay 0.0 --cond_mask_prob 0.1 --seed 10 --num_steps 600000 --save_interval 50000 --log_interval 1000 --eval_during_training --eval_split test --eval_batch_size 32 --eval_num_samples 1000 --eval_rep_times 3 --gen_during_training --gen_num_samples 3 --gen_num_repetitions 2 --gen_guidance_param 2.5 --train_platform_type TensorboardPlatform --overwrite

environment.persistence: All dependencies live on a 200GB RunPod network volume, so pod loss destroys only the running process, not the environment

deviations_from_reference.justification: Logging backend only. Avoids a third-party account dependency and keeps metrics on our volume.

deviations_from_reference.reference: args.json records 600000; the shipped checkpoint file is named model000750000.pt
deviations_from_reference.justification: Unresolved discrepancy. The reference may have been resumed and extended beyond its recorded config. We follow the recorded config.
The original environment is not installable on modern CUDA/sm_86. This is the single largest source of possible numerical divergence.

deviations_from_reference.change: linalg.sqrtm(X, disp=False) -> _sq = linalg.sqrtm(X); covmean = _sq[0] if isinstance(_sq, tuple) else _sq
deviations_from_reference.justification: scipy >=1.18 removed the disp kwarg. Old API returned (matrix, errest), new returns the matrix. Handles both; mathematically identical. Affects evaluation only, not training.

deviations_from_reference.change: Restore FigureCanvasAgg.tostring_rgb from buffer_rgba (drop alpha) when absent
deviations_from_reference.justification: matplotlib >=3.10 removed tostring_rgb, which moviepy 1.x calls in mplfig_to_npimage. Pixel-identical. Downgrading matplotlib is not viable because <3.8 does not support numpy 2. Affects sample rendering only.

preparation_gotchas_solved.symptom: ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 0) at dataset.py:289 - an error naming nothing relevant
preparation_gotchas_solved.root_cause: p7zip 16.02 (Ubuntu 22.04 default) cannot read RAR5. It exits 0 and creates all 29228 entries as 0-byte files. The dataset loader then swallows every resulting EOFError in a bare 'except: pass', leaving new_name_list empty.
preparation_gotchas_solved.also_failed: bsdtar/libarchive extracted ~9912 files then failed with 'Unsupported block header size'

preparation_gotchas_solved.symptom: texts/ directory absent after downloading the Drive folder
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'chumpy' when smplx unpickles SMPL_NEUTRAL.pkl
preparation_gotchas_solved.root_cause: chumpy setup.py does 'import pip', which fails under pip build isolation
preparation_gotchas_solved.note: Installs and imports cleanly as 0.71 on Python 3.12. This also retires the Rotation2xyz stub previously used in our inference server.

preflight_validation.purpose: Exercise the eval + generation + save code paths that only fire at save_interval, at tiny scale, so the 29h run cannot die at step 50000
artifacts_verified: checkpoints (model + optimizer state) written at every save_interval

sanity_metrics_observed.interpretation: Ground-truth values match published HumanML3D figures, confirming the evaluators loaded correctly. The untrained (step 0) model scores appropriately random, confirming the eval discriminates.

training_sanity.interpretation: Plausible early-training values; loss decreasing; higher loss at high-noise quartile q3 is expected

risks.risk: Crash at first save_interval because eval/gen paths untested
risks.mitigation: Pre-flight validation run passed; caught 2 real bugs
Checkpoints (model + optimizer state) every 50000 steps to the network volume; resume with --resume_checkpoint. On-demand (non-interruptible) instance chosen specifically to reduce this.
Launched under setsid nohup, fully detached; verified across all prior long-running jobs in this project

risks.risk: Numerical divergence from reference due to 4-year library version gap
risks.mitigation: Cannot be eliminated. Detected by acceptance criteria - this is precisely what the run is designed to surface.

risks.quantified: 12 checkpoints * 225MB (81.8MB model + 143MB optimizer) = 2.7GB, plus sample renders. Volume is 200GB with ~195GB free.

risks.risk: Cost overrun from idle finished pod
risks.mitigation: Known run duration (~31h); check on completion and stop the pod

risks.detail: 3090 stock is Low and EU-CZ-1 is the only datacenter carrying it (network volume is datacenter-locked). Fallback is RTX 4090 at $0.69/hr, which would change step timing.

monitoring: TensorBoard event files on the volume
execution.checkpoint_retention: keep all 12 - they are the evidence of the loss curve and allow post-hoc evaluation at any point in training

acceptance_criteria.note: The run is a TEST, so it needs a defined pass condition

quantitative_primary.method: Compare final-checkpoint T2M evaluator metrics against the reference checkpoint, evaluated identically on the test split
quantitative_primary.tolerance_confidence: LOW - this is a guess and is open_questions[0]. Diffusion training has run-to-run variance even at fixed seed (cuDNN non-determinism, different library versions).

acceptance_criteria.qualitative_secondary: Generate a fixed prompt set through both our checkpoint and the reference; compare behavioural equivalence in the viewer
acceptance_criteria.diagnostic_continuous: Loss curve shape should track the reference trajectory
acceptance_criteria.confound_handling: If our 600k result underperforms the reference, the most likely explanation is that the reference had 150k more steps, not that our pipeline is broken. Evaluating our own 550k checkpoint against our 600k one will show whether the curve had flattened - if it had, step count is not the explanation and something else differs.

open_questions.question: What FID / R-precision deltas should count as a successful reproduction, given a 4-year library-version gap?
600k (recorded config) or 750k (shipped checkpoint filename) steps?
open_questions.current_plan: 600k, running; a 150k continuation is planned as an option after this run rather than a restart
open_questions.verified_mechanism: num_epochs is computed from num_steps alone and ignores resume_step, so on a resume num_steps acts as ADDITIONAL steps on top of the resumed position. A prior run reaching ~150k, resumed with num_steps=600000, would run 600161 further steps and land at ~750161 - producing a checkpoint named model000750000.pt. This is arithmetically consistent with the reference.
open_questions.unresolved_caveat: The reference args.json records resume_checkpoint as empty string, which is inconsistent with that specific history. args.json is rewritten unconditionally on every launch (train_mdm.py:33-35, no resume guard), so a resuming launch WOULD have recorded its resume path. The mechanism is confirmed; the reference's exact training history is not.
open_questions.practical_consequence: Our run is a genuine from-scratch 600161 steps. If we later want to match 750k, resume from the final checkpoint with num_steps=150000, which will add ~150136 steps.

open_questions.question: Set torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True) and cudnn.deterministic?
open_questions.tradeoff: costs throughput but makes the run exactly re-runnable

open_questions.question: Is 12 full evals (1000 samples x 3 reps) the right cadence, or reduce eval_rep_times to 1 during training and do the full 3-rep evaluation once post-hoc from saved checkpoints?
open_questions.current_plan: full fidelity, 12 x (1000 x 3), per operator instruction not to cut corners

open_questions.question: Are any of the 5 listed deviations material rather than benign?
open_questions.current_plan: deviations 1, 4, 5 assessed benign; 2 and 3 assessed material
